headline: The US government paid psychics to spy on its enemies for almost 20 years.
slides: The Army set up a unit of psychic spies at Fort Meade, Maryland.
Their job: describe distant places and events they had never seen, using only their minds.
It ran under names like GRILL FLAME and SUN STREAK before the one that stuck: STAR GATE.
That is roughly what was spent on it and related work over more than two decades.
The program was handed to the CIA, which asked outside researchers to evaluate it.
The review found it had never been useful in an intelligence operation. It was cancelled and declassified.
sources: Sources: CIA Reading Room (STAR GATE collection), American Institutes for Research evaluation (Sept 29 1995), FAS
